items.problem: Migrated NavigationView/Frame shell does not scroll-host scenario content, so a page taller than the small capture window (~768x519) clips its bottom controls out of the render and UIA tree. Scenario7 Live Seekable Range scored partial (cov 10/19).
items.evidence: migration-score.json feature 'Live Seekable Range' verdict=partial ('bottom layout is cramped/truncated ... seek-offset buttons not found in UIA tree'); discrepancies.json severity=medium; migrated MainPage.xaml hosts <Frame x:Name="ScenarioFrame"/> under NavigationView with zero page-level ScrollViewer.
items.root_cause: WinUI 3 window is smaller than UWP's sample window and NavigationView/Frame content does not scroll; UWP's scrolling content host is lost in shell conversion, so tall pages clip.
items.change: Added Navigation invariant #5 to the Shell Conversion section: scroll-host the scenario content Frame in a ScrollViewer so pages taller than the window stay reachable, with a caveat that star-sized fill elements (e.g. MediaPlayerElement Height="*") need a MinHeight to avoid collapsing under the ScrollViewer's infinite measure.
items.expected_effect: Migrated shells wrap scenario content in a ScrollViewer; tall pages no longer clip their bottom controls, which then appear in the render and UIA tree.
items.falsifiable_check: On a re-run of a scenario with an over-tall page, all lower controls appear in the parity UIA tree and the feature goes partial->pass (e.g. Live Seekable Range coverage rises above 10/19).

deferred_to_human: MediaPlayerElement exposes no AutomationId and two Set buttons without AutomationId can't be auto-invoked by winui3-parity-check (UIA). This is an eval-skill/UIA measurement limitation, not a migration-skill fix; recorded for human review, not auto-applied.
Consider whether the parity/capture window size (~768x519) should be enlarged in the harness to better match UWP's default sample window (tier-0 / harness, out of scope here).
